title: Bitcoin mining industry developments and energy usage trends
content:
TL;DR: As of February 05, 2026, Bitcoin's network hums with 905.84 EH/s of hashpower, securing a difficulty of 146.47 T, proving its unyielding resilience. With 82.0% progress towards the next adjustment and 363 blocks remaining, transactors should monitor for potential shifts in mining profitability and transaction costs. This relentless computational effort is the bedrock of individual monetary sovereignty, insulating wealth from the arbitrary whims of central authorities.

The Report

As of February 05, 2026, at 02:21 UTC, the Bitcoin network continues its unwavering march towards immutable financial truth. The current block height stands at 935,061, a testament to over a decade of continuous, uninterrupted operation. The network is fully OPERATIONAL, a consistent beacon in a world of increasingly fragile financial systems. Powering this decentralized leviathan is a formidable hashrate of 905.84 Exahashes per second (EH/s). This immense computational force, while slightly below the approximate 977 EH/s observed in late January 2026, still represents a staggering global commitment to securing the hardest money ever created. It is crucial to note that this current difficulty, standing at 146.47 T, is not an all-time high, remaining below the November 2025 peak of 155.9 T. This distinction underscores the dynamic, self-correcting nature of Bitcoin's difficulty adjustment mechanism, which adapts to changes in global mining power rather than perpetually escalating.

The gears of this self-regulating system are already turning towards the next recalibration. The difficulty adjustment process is 82.0% complete, with just 363 blocks remaining until the network reassesses the computational effort required to mine new blocks.
